title: RISE: Adaptive Imagination for World Action Models
why: Directly allocates rollout depth through sequential Roll/Stop decisions that compare expected planning benefit with compute cost, making it the closest missing mechanism and a mandatory novelty boundary.

title: VLA-ATTC: Adaptive Test-Time Compute for VLA Models with Relative Action Critic Model
why: Implements adaptive test-time compute for manipulation by uncertainty-triggered candidate generation and relative action criticism, so the proposed decision-change criterion must beat this excluded gating-and-reranking baseline.

title: When and How Much to Imagine: Adaptive Test-Time Scaling with World Models for Visual Spatial Reasoning
why: Selectively invokes and scales world-model calls and language tokens from evidence sufficiency, providing the closest cross-domain adaptive-imagination formulation even though it does not target executed manipulation actions.

title: DREAMSTEER: Latent World Models Can Steer VLA Policies During Deployment Without Any Finetuning
why: Uses a frozen VLA plus latent world model to imagine and value-rank candidate action chunks at deployment, forming the load-bearing fixed-budget candidate-search baseline for any adaptive candidate-count claim.

title: When to Trust Imagination: Adaptive Action Execution for World Action Models
why: Adapts executed chunk length through future-reality verification rather than allocating imagination compute, making it the essential adaptive-chunking exclusion and efficiency comparator.

title: CheckVLA: Execution-Time Verification with Action-Conditioned World Model for Long-Horizon Mobile Manipulation
why: A frozen action-conditioned world model drives calibrated execution-time intervention and repair, supplying the strongest recent verification-gating boundary distinct from decision-adaptive imagination depth.

title: Fast-WAM: Do World Action Models Need Test-time Future Imagination?
why: Separates video co-training from inference-time imagination and shows a no-imagination alternative, so it is the necessary zero-compute counter-hypothesis for claims that selective rollout adds action value.

title: DreamWAM: Beyond RGB Future Prediction for World Action Models
why: Introduces structured future modalities beyond RGB and therefore supplies a concrete high-fidelity imagination endpoint against which dynamic representation-fidelity allocation must be tested.
